==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|disordre||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{bor+|en|frm|desordre}} (modern {{cog|fr|désordre}}), from {{der|en|fro|desordre}}, from {{af|fro|des-|ordre|nocat=1}}; {{surf|en|dis-|order|nocap=1}} (<< {{der|en|la|ōrdō}}).

Compare typologically {{m+|ru|непоря́док}}, {{m|ru|беспоря́док}}, {{m|ru|неуря́дица}} (akin to {{m|ru|ряд}}, {{m|ru|поря́док}}).

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/dɪsˈɔːdə(ɹ)/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/dɪsˈɔɹdɚ/|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/dɪzˈɔːɹdəɹ/<q:obsolete><ref:{{R:Jespersen MEGoHP|I|6.64|203}}>}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-disorder.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)də(ɹ)|s=3}}
* {{hyph|en|dis|or|der}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# [[absence|Absence]] of [[order]]; state of not being arranged in an orderly manner.
#: {{ux|en|After playing the children left the room in '''disorder'''.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1986
|author=w:John le Carré
|title=w:A Perfect Spy
|section=
|passage= It was a household in permanent and benevolent  '''disorder''', pervaded by the gentle thrill of religious persecution.}}
# {{sid|en|disturbance}} A [[disturbance]] of [[civic]] [[peace]] or of [[public]] [[order]].
#: {{ux|en|The class was thrown into '''disorder''' when the teacher left the room}}
#: {{ux|en|The army tried to prevent '''disorder''' when claims the elections had been rigged grew stronger.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q12136}} {{lb|en|medicine|countable}} A [[physical]] or [[mental]] [[malfunction]].
#: {{nearsyn|en|disease<id:Q12136>|illness<id:Q12136><qq:both often synonymous><!--i.e., often not differentiated in usage-->}}
#: {{ux|en|[[bulimia|Bulimia]] is an eating '''disorder'''.}}

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|absence of order}} {{l|en|chaos}}, {{l|en|entropy}}; see also [[Thesaurus:disorder]]
* {{sense|disturbance of civic peace}} See also [[Thesaurus:riot]]

====Hyponyms====
''See [[Thesaurus:disorder/hyponyms]]''
